title: Machine-learning-derived seven-protein panel distinguishes remission from active ANCA-associated vasculitis
summary: Confounder-aware machine-learning feature selection on plasma proteomics identified a seven-protein signature—AHSG, CLEC3B, COMP, F9, LRG1, MCAM and MRC1—to classify remission versus active ANCA-associated vasculitis (AAV). After targeted PRM mass-spectrometry assay development, a generalized linear model was evaluated in an independent cohort of 108 AAV patients and achieved AUC 0.94 (95% CI 0.90–0.98); combined discovery and validation performance was AUC 0.97. In the study cohorts, the panel outperformed routine CRP and ANCA titer measurements.
ai_technology: MetaDeconfoundR confounder-aware feature analysis, LASSO and Boruta feature selection, and a generalized linear model applied to targeted PRM mass-spectrometry data
organization: Max Delbrück Center for Molecular Medicine; Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin; Berlin Institute of Health; Charles University and General University Hospital Prague; University of Oslo

evidence.tested: After targeted PRM mass-spectrometry assay development, a generalized linear model was evaluated in an independent cohort of 108 AAV patients and achieved AUC 0.94 (95% CI 0.90–0.98); combined discovery and validation performance was AUC 0.97.
evidence.unknown: This is cross-sectional classification of disease state in patients already diagnosed with AAV, not a prospective prediction of relapse, a validated basis for stopping immunosuppression, or evidence of improved clinical outcomes. The two cohorts together included just over 200 patients with a rare disease; the authors note uncertainty from sample size and treatment heterogeneity, and the panel remains a starting point for clinical-tool development. It is an adjunct biomarker result, not proof that the seven proteins cause remission or vasculitis activity.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning methods accounted for clinical covariates including CRP, kidney function and ANCA-related measures, prioritized candidate plasma proteins, and reduced these to a seven-protein panel. Targeted PRM-MS quantified the selected proteins, and the GLM classified AAV remission versus active disease in an independent cohort. The measured validation performance and protein signature are the specific AI-enabled diagnostic finding.
